title: DevOps Center - The New Deployment Tool - Sigma Infosolutions
body: # DevOps Center – The New Deployment Tool. DevOps Center, a recent addition to Salesforce applications, is designed to eventually replace change sets in its functionalities. The game-changer for Salesforce teams is that the DevOps Center manages the source control branch so you can focus on development tasks. However, it’s important to note that eventually, Salesforce is likely to retire change sets altogether in favor of the DevOps Center. **DevOps Center** significantly improves the change and release management process when developing with Salesforce. * **Organize your work:** Work Items, a new object designed for the DevOps Center and open to standard Salesforce Flows and other operations, can be used to track and deploy the associated changes. **Creating a new Work Item**. ## Work Item Stages:. Work Item Stages in DevOps Center Salesforce are the different phases that a work item goes through as it is developed, tested, and deployed to production. When you click ‘Create Review,’ the work item transitions to the ‘In Review’ status, and an automatic change request is generated. This work item advances to a pipeline stage, and upon reaching the final stage, it transitions to the Closed status. To incorporate metadata changes into the Work Item, you have two alternatives:. Clicking it transitions the Work Item to the ‘**In Review**‘ stage, simultaneously creating a pull request in the backend. After initiating a pull request, you can designate it as ‘**Ready to Promote**,’ enabling the Work Item for promotion to the next stage in the pipeline. And there you have it, the Work Item has been successfully deployed! After a successful promotion, the Work Item will transition automatically to the **Closed** stage. ## Change Work Item Status to Never:. If a change conflicts, removing files from the commit can ensure successful promotions of other work items. When you change the status to Never, the work item becomes inactive, and the committed component files are returned to the list of available changes. You can change a work item’s status to Never before it’s been promoted into a pipeline stage. From the work item menu, select **Change Status to Never**, then click **Confirm**.

title: Who's Buying the Future of AI & Robotics
body:
Private funding set records too. According to the PitchBook-NVCA Venture Monitor, U.S. venture funding reached $515.8 billion in the first nine months of 2026. That is about 44% above 2021’s full-year record, and AI took 82.7% of it.

Physical AI drew some of the largest private rounds. In the wider industry, Waymo raised $16 billion for autonomous driving and Skild AI raised $1.4 billion for general-purpose robot AI. SoftBank Group (9984.T), a ROBO and THNQ member, led the Skild AI round. [...] After several years of cooling appetite for M&A and large IPOs, 2026 has seen a resurgence in both, as well as increased appetite for venture fundraising in robotics and physical AI. Notably, on November 2, Marvell Technology (MRVL) agreed to combine with Lumentum (LITE) for about $115 billion, a month after its investor day lifted its connectivity outlook. Our report tracks deals across the ROBO Global Robotics and Automation Index (ROBO), the ROBO Global Artificial Intelligence Index (THNQ) [...] It has been a record-setting year in many ways. Most notably, two records came from SpaceX (SPCX). First, its February merger with xAI valued the combined company at about $1.25 trillion, the largest merger on record. Second, its June listing then raised about $75 billion, the largest IPO ever. Furthermore, we’ve seen the most deal activity overall since 2021 (surpassing that, even), with just under two months remaining.

title: Promoting the Development of the Semiconductor Ecosystem in Viet Nam | OECD
body: The semiconductor industry, the backbone of modern digital and electronic technologies, is witnessing significant shifts in its global landscape. The high concentration of critical segments of the semiconductor value chain in a limited number of regions increases vulnerability to disruptions. In this changing landscape, economies are seeking to enhance the resilience of the semiconductor value chain through the development of local ecosystems and by strengthening their role in this [...] Building on its strong industrial base, substantial foreign investment, increasing policy prioritisation, growing pool of technical talent and deep integration into global value chains, Viet Nam is well positioned to strengthen its role in the global semiconductor industry. Effective implementation of current policy commitments, combined with sustained investment in innovation, infrastructure and human capital, will be essential to achieving the country’s long-term semiconductor ambitions: [...] Viet Nam has emerged as an increasingly important participant in global semiconductor value chains with ambitious objectives to further develop its semiconductor ecosystem. This report analyses the opportunities, challenges and policy levers supporting the development of Viet Nam’s semiconductor ecosystem and identifies policy recommendations to support the ecosystem’s development.
